_comment: Already-MERGED migrations that fail squawk and can no longer be fixed.
This is NOT grandfathered-migrations.json. That file is a fixed snapshot of
what existed before the zero-downtime guard landed (2026-07-16) and its
meaning must stay exactly that. This file is the escape hatch for the other
case: a migration written AFTER the guard that merged red anyway.
Why the hatch has to exist. Migrations are immutable (CI job 'Migrations are
immutable' rejects any edit to a merged file), and squawk lints file TEXT, so
a finding in a merged migration cannot be fixed by a follow-up migration. But
squawk's target set is every non-exempt file, not just the ones a PR adds --
so one red merge fails the lint on every unrelated PR from then on. Without a
waiver the only ways out are to corrupt the grandfather snapshot's meaning or
to leave the gate red for everybody.
Adding an entry here is DEBT, not absolution: the finding is real and it
shipped. Every entry states what is wrong and why it is unfixable, and
squawk-lint prints the whole list on each run so it cannot go quiet.
Adding a NEW migration here is almost always the wrong move -- fix the file
in the PR that adds it, while it is still mutable.

files.reason: Merged with the squawk check red. Three findings: no lock_timeout and no statement_timeout before ALTER TABLE kortix.credit_accounts ADD COLUMN (require-timeout-settings x2), and a DROP COLUMN in its 'Down Migration' section (ban-drop-column).
files.unfixableBecause: The file is merged and immutable, and squawk lints file text -- no follow-up migration can clear a finding in it.
files.rootCauseFixed: scripts/generate.ts now prepends the safety header that scripts/create-migration.ts always had, so drizzle-generated migrations no longer start life missing the timeouts. The repo does not write 'Down Migration' sections (see create-migration.ts); this file's was hand-added.
files.realRisk: ADD COLUMN with a constant DEFAULT does not rewrite the table on PG11+, but it still takes a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. With no lock_timeout that ALTER waits behind any long transaction on credit_accounts and every query queues behind it. This has run on dev; it has NOT run on prod yet.

files.reason: Merged with the squawk check red. One finding: the drizzle-generated FK name capture_enrollments_token_id_capture_enrollment_tokens_token_id_fk is 66 bytes, so PostgreSQL truncates it to 63 bytes (identifier-too-long).
files.unfixableBecause: The file is merged and immutable, and squawk lints file text -- no follow-up migration can clear a finding in it.
files.rootCauseFixed: Not fixed. A pull request into dev runs no squawk job, and pnpm test does not run squawk-lint, so a red migration reaches dev unseen and surfaces first on the staging promotion. Run `pnpm migrate:lint:squawk` before merging a migration.
files.realRisk: Cosmetic. The constraint exists as capture_enrollments_token_id_capture_enrollment_tokens_token_id; the drizzle snapshots keep the 66-byte name. No code references the name. A future DROP CONSTRAINT must use the truncated name. The table is new in this release and has not run on staging or prod.

files.reason: Merged with the squawk check red. Five findings: ALTER COLUMN user_id DROP NOT NULL on kortix.capture_devices, timeline_actions, timeline_audio, timeline_chunks and timeline_frames (ban-drop-not-null x5).
files.unfixableBecause: The file is merged and immutable, and squawk lints file text -- no follow-up migration can clear a finding in it.
files.rootCauseFixed: Not fixed. A pull request into dev runs no squawk job, and pnpm test does not run squawk-lint, so a red migration reaches dev unseen and surfaces first on the staging promotion. Run `pnpm migrate:lint:squawk` before merging a migration.
files.realRisk: None for old clients. The five tables ship with Capture in the same release (no migration for them exists on staging or prod), so no deployed reader assumes user_id is NOT NULL; the file's mixed-version-safe line records this. DROP NOT NULL is a catalog-only change with no rewrite or scan.
